messages:
anya: heads up — I'm seeing nondeterministic eval scores on quant-red-1 when running the harness with a fixed seed. runs with `--seed 1234` bounce between 0.784 and 0.803 for exact-match.

sam: that's annoying. does it repro locally if you run the same command twice?

anya: yes. i ran this 6x on my laptop and on CI. same docker image, same commit hash. only difference is workers >1. command: `./tools/eval --model quant-red-1 --seed 1234 --batch 16 --workers 4 --streaming`

julia: are you certain the seed is being applied to all RNGs? we have both the C++ PRNG in the runtime and the python-level numpy/random state for some samplers.

anya: I thought so. logs show the harness seed set at start: `INFO EvalRunner: global_seed=1234`. but look at worker logs (snippet):
```
worker-2: init rng seed=1234
worker-2: sampling start: sampler_id=async-token-sampler state=0x7f9a3c2b
worker-2: generated token 0x1f4a -> 42
...
worker-2: sampling complete
worker-2: next task received WITHOUT reseed
```

anya: that "WITHOUT reseed" line was my local debug print I added. seems like worker pool reuses the PRNG state between tasks when async sampler yields.

devon: oh interesting — we changed the worker reuse behavior in the async sampler PR (PR #812) to avoid reinitializing between tiny tasks for perf. looks like we accidentally relied on per-task reseed semantics.

sam: so per-task determinism was a contract. if worker reuse keeps state, sequence of tasks matters. CI parallelism might change ordering => nondet.

julia: can you try forcing `--workers 1` and `--streaming false` to isolate? if that stabilizes scores then it's the worker-state leak.

anya: `--workers 1` + `--streaming false` => stable 0.797 across runs. with workers>1 and streaming we get the bounce.

devon: quick mitigation: we can add explicit reseed at task start based on `global_seed + task_index` so order-independent. downside: cost of reseed for every short task.

sam: +1 on deterministic fix, but also let's add a regression test in eval CI that runs the same prompt N times with fixed seed and asserts mean/std below a tiny threshold. CI job: `eval-determinism-quick` flagged this morning (job 1452).

anya: i'll open an issue and PR with both fixes: (1) reseed-per-task (config flag off by default but on for eval harness), (2) unit test for repeated-run determinism. GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/issues/298 — draft PR coming.

eval-bot: CI job 1452 has flaky failures linked to nondeterministic evals — tagging engineers: @sam @anya

julia: tiny note — when using quantized kernels, tiny floating differences can amplify under sampling, but that shouldn't flip exact-match this much if seed is fixed. so probably not only quantization noise.

devon: agree. this smells like PRNG carryover. i'll review the async sampler PR and mark the lines that skip reseed. if we revert that micro-optimization we should be safe until we implement a deterministic pooling strategy.

sam: can we also log a short RNG fingerprint at task boundary in CI (e.g., a hash of the first 8 random bytes) so we can correlate ordering differences across runs?

anya: good idea — adding `rng_fingerprint=<hex>` to eval logs. will include in the PR.

julia: ok thanks, team. priority: patch in eval repo + CI test. devon please coordinate with eng-sre if we need to re-run recent dedicated capacity jobs for verification.

devon: will do. assigning myself to the GH issue and will ping eng-sre when the PR is ready for staged rollout.

anya: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/301 (WIP) — includes repro script and logs.

sam: awesome — ping here when CI passes and we can close the incident. :thumbsup:
